title: Membranes in dairy plants foul quickly and need cleaning every week.

record.text: Membranes in dairy plants foul quickly and need cleaning every week.
record.detail: At two dairy plants we service — one near Temerin, one outside Bečej — our MBR membranes are fouling much faster than the design assumptions. We scheduled cleaning cycles every two weeks, but in practice the operators are forced to do a full CIP clean every five to seven days because transmembrane pressure spikes. A full CIP uses roughly 200 litres of citric acid and caustic solution per unit and takes the system offline for four to six hours. That adds up to significant chemical cost and lost treatment capacity over a year. We have tried adjusting aeration intensity and sludge retention time, but the fouling rate has not changed much. Dairy wastewater has high fats, proteins, and sugars, and we think the combination is forming a gel layer the biology is not breaking down fast enough. We do not have the tools or know-how to characterise the foulant properly. Our service records go back three years and show a clear seasonal pattern — fouling is worst in summer, which might point to temperature effects on the biology or on the fat chemistry. A good outcome would be a reliable explanation of what is causing the fouling and a practical change — to pre-treatment, aeration, or membrane material — that pushes cleaning intervals back to at least twelve days.
